html:
Caral-Supe was a cluster of some thirty towns with monumental mounds and sunken plazas on the north-central coast of Peru, flourishing from about 3000 BCE to about 1800 BCE. It is the oldest known civilisation in the Americas, and one of the few places on Earth where civilisation arose on its own.

The towns sat along three short rivers running down from the Andes to the Pacific: the Fortaleza, the Pativilca and the Supe. The best studied is the city of Caral in the Supe valley. Archaeologists also call the whole culture Norte Chico, "the little north".

What makes it strange is what it lacked. There was no pottery, no known writing and almost no surviving art. Yet its people raised large stepped platform mounds and circular plazas, which took organised labour on a big scale. Their economy seems to have joined two zones: farmers inland grew cotton, squash and beans with river irrigation, while fishers on the coast caught anchovies and sardines with cotton nets. Knotted strings found at Caral may be an early form of the quipu.

For scale: it rose about a thousand years after the Sumerian city-states, at the same time as the pyramids of Old Kingdom Egypt, and nearly two thousand years before the Olmecs of Mexico. Building declined after about 1800 BCE, and the centre of Andean religion and power later moved inland, to places like Chavín.
